Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

zcvel and the pit-filling increment were parameter(4.2) and a literal 1.0 in two copies, landmod's roffini and glaciermod's oroini, of which oroini is the one that survives. Both now derive from landmod_nl keys: zcvel = roffvel*ga**(0.5-roffexp) and zoroinc = roffpit*ga. Because zoro is geopotential, that makes the velocity proportional to sqrt(ga) once the slope is divided back to a topographic one, which is the open-channel scaling; the exponent is written as (0.5-roffexp) so the two cannot drift apart. roffvel = 2.022845 reproduces 4.200 at ga = 9.80665, and roffpit = 0.101972 m reproduces 1.000 m2/s2, so an Earth configuration is unchanged -- an identity that can fail. At this planet's gravity the effective zcvel is 4.575, 1.0893x upstream's, which is the 1.14x from sqrt(g) less the 1.049x the geopotential slope was already supplying.

Both densities are DECLARED AS INHERITED with the bracket reported, which is the second arm of the acceptance criterion. rhosnow joins landmod_nl and rhoglac joins glacier_nl, values unchanged at 330 and 850 kg/m3, so the bracket can now be RUN rather than only stated. The declaration beside each says what the constant does -- rhosnow converts water equivalent to the physical snow thickness that insulates the soil column, rhoglac to the ice thickness that enters the orography -- and that both are settled densities set by overburden compaction, which scales with gravity, so both are low on a planet whose surface gravity is 1.306x the one they were measured on. Not rescaled: firn densification is not a closed-form function of gravity that can be evaluated here, and this project brackets an estimate it cannot verify rather than guessing it. The bracket is the issue's own, roughly 10 to 20 per cent on snow insulation thickness and on glacier relief. glaciermod already had the GRAVITY right in the orography conversion, with its own comment; the density beside it is the half that is inherited, and that is now said where the two meet.

SIMBA stays OFF -- nothing enables it and nveg is untouched. Both traps are disarmed rather than recorded. Trap 1: vegini now REFUSES nveg = 2 with nstartemp = 1 and stops, because vegstep sets dalb and not dsalb, so under a two-band shortwave SIMBA's vegetation albedo would reach the radiation nowhere while its roughness and its soil water bucket reached it everywhere. The positive form is a per-band vegetation albedo and there is no derivation for one, so the refusal is the decision procedure until there is. Trap 2: 'dwmax(jhor) = zwmax' is gated on NVEGWMAX, a new vegmod_nl key, and vegini states at initialisation which field owns the soil water bucket. The default is 1 -- SIMBA, upstream's behaviour, preserved exactly -- so nothing changes for anyone running it today, but a run can now keep the pedology-derived staged code-229 field instead of having it silently overwritten every timestep. The module header carries both items and, separately, the Earth calibrations that are approximate rather than broken: rlue against dfd(:,NLEP), the BROADBAND downward shortwave, rather than the photosynthetically active fraction; ct_crit's linear ramp from TMELT with no optimum and no high-temperature cutoff; q10's 283.16 K reference; Harvey's beta factor; the biome fits; and vsalb_min as a THIRD independent forested-snow albedo constant, now inconsistent with landmod's albforest masking as well as with the spectrum. Deletion was considered as the alternative and not taken: surfmod, plasimmod, the restart records and the output code table all reference the module, so removing it is a cross-batch change rather than a fix.

The two endmembers are re-weighted by the same derivation the third went through and moved to the same place. analysis/vegetation_albedo.py gains COVER_ENDMEMBERS and writes cover_albedo, cover_albedo_earth_sun and cover_albedo_bracket; config/planet.yaml gains model.tree_albedo 0.143 (from 0.13) and model.grass_albedo 0.209 (from 0.19) with brackets [0.130, 0.148] and [0.190, 0.217]; and build_surface_albedo.py's two flags default to the config with no silent Earth-Sun fallback, which is the rule --vegetation-albedo already followed. The POPULATION leaf ratio 1.1002 rather than the per-class one: tree and grass differ by 0.006 in ratio and 0.001 in albedo, and the grass class has four spectra in it, so a per-class ratio would not resolve the effect it claims to separate. lib/provenance.py: the two keys and their brackets join the inert sets of the three builders that never read them, and are deliberately absent from surface_albedo's, which does; check_consistency's re-grep confirms both halves. Discovered and filed as world-36g rather than fixed here: --mode modelled still writes ONE identical field to codes 174, 175 and 176, because the band split SPEC-5 added is gated on --mode vegetated, and splitting the modelled blend needs a band pair for the rock table that does not exist.

Fixed in 1b9aa183. Both literals are rainmod_nl keys. clwhsc, the e-folding length coefficient, DERIVES from the model's own gascon and ga (700*(gascon/ga)/(287.0/9.80665), returning 700 at Earth's values) because it is a length and the heights it is measured against are already built that way; a positive namelist value overrides. clwref, the reference in-cloud liquid density, is exposed UNCHANGED at Kiehl's value: it is a condensate concentration with no gravity dependence, so no consistency argument moves it, and its bracket is world-8h6. This CHANGES RESULTS -- thinner high cloud, slightly thicker low cloud, simulated mean down on both the longwave trap and the shortwave reflection -- and is recorded as an unpriced row in forcing-bundle-predictions.md, because pricing needs a baseline climatology and config declares none. cpl_stub.f90 rewritten: clsgini, clsgstep and clsgstop now declare exactly what cpl.f90 declares and what oceanmod.f90 and plasim_dummy.f90 pass, and each calls mpabort. CRHOS, CPS and CLFI are icemod_nl keys; icemod passes all four salinity constants into oceanini so the two modules cannot hold different sea water, and oceanmod's own parameter copies are gone. CONSUMERS ENUMERATED: CPS reaches (a) the mixed-layer heat capacity CRHOS*CPS in mksst, mkiflux, addfc, mkfc and the entropy diagnostics, and through mkiflux's residual flux it reaches ice growth as well as the SST tendency; icemod's own CPS was declared and never used, and is now the source of truth it passes down. CRHOS additionally is the snow-ice flooding threshold in subsnow as CRHOS-CRHOI. CLFI appears only as CRHOI*CLFI, latent heat per m3 of ice, in icestep, mkice, mkflukoi, addfci and oceanmod's addfc. CRHOF is declared in icemod and used nowhere. VALUES: CPS's compiled default corrected from 4180 (fresh water at about 25 C) to 3990.34 (sea water at S=34.7 and its freezing point); CRHOS and CLFI keep their compiled defaults and are only exposed. run_exoplasim derives CRHOS and CPS from config's salinity by EOS-80 and the UNESCO (1983) polynomial, each checked against published check values and against the constant CPS replaces; CLFI is declared in config because it depends on the ice's own salinity and temperature and the model has no such variable. All four go through configure_otherargs, so they survive a continuation, and through expected_namelist_keys. At the declared salinity the run configuration moves to CRHOS 1027.94 and CPS 3990.33: mixed-layer heat capacity down 5.1 per cent, so a declared 50 m mixed layer is 50 m of sea water rather than 52.5, and the flooding margin CRHOS-CRHOI from 110 to 107.94. Every run and climatology on disk is superseded (rule 7). Commit 9c952a18.

A cold start with no codes 169/210/211 now begins from a DECLARED profile or refuses to begin. read_ice_surface no longer constructs ice cover from the SST sentinel; make_ice_thickness's CCM3 relation is reachable only when a real cover was read, and warns that it is Earth-fitted and hemispherically asymmetric. ice_cold_start takes either the read climatology or icemod_nl's tsst_eq/tsst_pol/hice_ini profile, tsst_pol + (tsst_eq-tsst_pol)*cos(lat)**2, symmetric by construction, and aborts if neither exists. oceanmod's yclsst gains its -999 initialiser (module-scope SAVE, which -finit-real does not reach) and the ocean starts from the declared profile rather than from memory clipped to freezing. xicecc is set from the initial cover on BOTH paths, which is the fix for sic being identically zero beside a non-zero sit: mkicec only grows it and icestep copies it into xicec every step. config/planet.yaml declares ocean.cold_start and run_exoplasim writes TSST_EQ/TSST_POL/HICE_INI on a prepare and on every resume; expected_namelist_keys checks them. The declared cold start is ice-free, which is the side of the hysteresis the flux sweep could not reach; an arm that wants the iced side declares a sub-freezing pole or a non-zero thickness. WHAT DEPENDED ON THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: all 9 runs in exoplasim/runs cold-started from the constructed field and the ocean at freezing, and every restart carries it forward; per rule 7 the canonical climatology lineage does not exist, so all of it is disposable. NO RESTART RECORD ADDED OR CHANGED. Commit b5918b94.

nfluko cannot relax toward a constructed field: it is refused outright when there is no read climatology, on the -999 sentinel in xclsst/yclsst, which is a restart record so a continuation that switches nfluko on is refused the same way a cold start is. nfluko=1's two correction fields, codes 709 and 903, get sentinels of their own so 'absent' is not read as 'zero everywhere'. The same refusal covers the three other branches that prescribe rather than integrate a surface: nice=0, ntskin=0 and oceanmod's nocean=0. VERIFIED, not assumed: every consumer of the constructed field enumerated by grep over icemod.f90 and oceanmod.f90. Guarded by the abort - icestep's nice==0 block, its nfluko==1 block (xicec from xclicec2, and the xmaxd clause), mkflukoi, addfci, oceanmod's addfc, mkfc, getflxco and the nocean==0 block. Clamped harmless - iceget's AMAX1 makes xclicec2/xcliced2 zero, which is what iceout codes 790/791 and oceanstep's pcliced argument then see; xflxice2 and yfsst2 are set to zero on the nfluko==0 branch. Diagnostic only - the nprint==2 blocks, and ocean output code 990 which emits the sentinel and is in no pyburn code table and read by no script here. Dead - mkicecf is never called. Nothing else reads them. scripts/error_budget.py's no-q-flux item now records that a q-flux is not available on this world at any price. analysis/error_budget.json is absent from this tree and needs a baseline climatology, so it picks the text up on its next run. Commits b5918b94, 3a368340.

zh0 is now icemod_nl's HLEAD, declared in config at ExoPlaSim's value: exposed, not changed, and it reproduces the compiled 0.5 exactly. It was a local in both mkicec (live) and mkicecf (dead) and both now read the module value. getiflx is DELETED. The thickness limit's melt is paid out of the same cell's conductive flux to the ocean instead of a global area-weighted sum spread over every other cell with ice below the limit; the old form was a heat transport with no carrier and it also dropped the remainder silently whenever demand exceeded capacity, since xcfluxr is reset at the top of every icestep. xmaxd is DECLARED OFF (-1.0) in config/planet.yaml and written to the namelist, so the branch cannot fire in any arm. The argument: 9 m is Earth's Arctic multi-year maximum standing in for ice export, which this model does not have and which the error budget already carries as a declared structural term; and xmaxd is not only a clamp, because mkcflux and skintemp zero the conductive flux once ice reaches it, so a positive value stops basal growth outright. Conductive growth goes as the square root of time, so switching it off leaves nothing unbounded. Dormant at the current climate, so the baseline is unchanged. XMAXD and HLEAD are both in configure_otherargs and expected_namelist_keys. Commit 9e6372e1.

albedo_mode now takes the endmember from source_config.model.land_albedo_source on the run's own manifest, with no fallback; the land-mean albedo is still measured from the run's staged SRA and reported beside it. Added a check that fails when two arms at one flux were handed the same land-mean albedo. Verified: the old rule returns 'vegetated' for both of today's endmembers; the new one returns 'lithology' for a lithology manifest and raises where the declaration is absent. Every run on disk declares vegetated, so 'cannot bracket' is now a true statement about the run set.
